chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Bakr al-Hazrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) prescribed zakat upon nine things: wheat, barley, dates, raisins, gold, silver, camels, cattle, and sheep — and pardoned [everything] besides that.'

Yunus said: 'The meaning of his statement that zakat is on nine things and pardons what is besides that — this was only during the beginning of prophethood, just as the salat used to be two cycles (rak'at), then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) added seven cycles to it. Likewise, zakat: he established it and made it a sunnah at the beginning of his prophethood upon nine things, then he extended it to all grains.'

key_terms.الزَّكَاة: zakat — the obligatory alms-tax, one of the pillars of Islam, here referring to the gradual development of its scope during the prophetic mission
key_terms.النُّبُوَّة: prophethood (nubuwwa) — the period of divine mission, here specifically the 'beginning of prophethood' when initial regulations were revealed
key_terms.الْحُبُوب: grains (hubb pl. hubub) — the broader category to which zakat was eventually extended beyond the original nine items
key_terms.الْحِنْطَة: wheat — one of the foundational grains subject to zakat
key_terms.رَكْعَة: rak'a — a unit/cycle of the salat prayer, used as an analogy to illustrate the gradual expansion of religious law
key_terms.سَنَّ: to institute as sunnah — to establish a practice as a normative precedent

ai.seo_question: On what nine things did the Prophet Muhammad prescribe zakat according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith reports Imam al-Sadiq's (AS) narration that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) originally prescribed zakat on only nine items — wheat, barley, dates, raisins, gold, silver, camels, cattle, and sheep. The narrator Yunus then provides an important jurisprudential clarification: this initial nine-item ruling was specific to the early period of prophethood, analogous to the salat initially being two cycles before being expanded to more. The Prophet later extended zakat to cover all grains, showing that certain Islamic rulings were revealed and developed progressively, not all at once.
